stories.title: FRC roadmap to make firms disclose emissions, sustainability performance
stories.summary: The Financial Reporting Council is set to unveil a roadmap for mandatory sustainability reporting in Bangladesh. Local companies will face binding rules in phases over the next six to seven years. The top 50 listed firms may be the first to disclose performance alongside financial results.

stories.title: JBM Auto submits FY26 Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report
stories.summary: JBM Auto has filed its FY26 Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report with the Bombay and National Stock Exchanges. The company reported a decrease in energy consumption and Scope 2 emissions for the period. Vinay and Keshava LLP provided limited assurance on the data.

stories.title: Lupin ranks 318th on TIME and Statista sustainability list
stories.summary: Lupin Limited has been ranked 318th on TIME and Statista's World's Most Sustainable Companies 2026 list. The selection process evaluated firms on more than 20 sustainability indicators. The company previously earned a CDP A rating for climate change and water security.

stories.title: Southwire Recognized Among America's Greenest Companies for 2027 - StreetInsider
Wiley releases fiscal 2026 sustainability report
stories.summary: Wiley has released its FY26 sustainability report, claiming a 28 percent reduction in emissions since 2020. CEO Matthew Kissner stated the company's role is to protect the integrity of knowledge and ensure innovation is sustainable. The report highlights the firm's ongoing stewardship efforts.

stories.title: COP31: New UN framework puts businesses’ net-zero progress on public record
stories.summary: The United Nations has unveiled a reporting tool at COP31 allowing corporations and governments to place climate targets on a public register. Eighty entities have opted in so far. Market observers remain sceptical of voluntary mechanisms that distinguish between published intentions and actual delivery.

stories.title: SAP stock gains sustainability detail with new cloud emissions views
stories.summary: SAP is providing customers with new views on the energy use and emissions linked to their cloud services. The company continues to use spend-based estimates as its primary reporting reference for cloud emissions. The update adds a sustainability angle to the firm's cloud expansion story.

stories.title: Consultation on sustainability reporting assurance standards opens
stories.summary: The European Commission has launched a consultation on draft standards for the independent assurance of corporate sustainability reporting. The move concerns the limited assurance requirement under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive. Large companies are required to disclose sustainability performance and obtain external verification.

stories.title: Corporate sustainability reports face scrutiny as EU drafts oversight standards - The Brussels Times
Bremenports publishes first sustainability report under European VSME standard
stories.summary: Bremenports has released its 2026 sustainability report, titled Responsibility for the Ports of Tomorrow. For the first time, the document follows the European Voluntary Sustainability Reporting Standard for SMEs. It covers the 2024 and 2025 financial years for the port management company.

stories.title: EU Commission releases draft sustainability reporting assurance standards
stories.summary: The European Commission has announced a consultation on a draft standard for the limited assurance of sustainability reporting. The initiative aims to support consistency across the EU's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive framework. Companies are required to obtain assurance through an independent external reviewer.

stories.title: Singapore authorises first Rwanda carbon credit project at COP31
stories.summary: Singapore has authorised its first carbon credit project under its national framework, a water filter scheme in Rwanda. Developed by Climate Bridge International, the project aims to distribute 300,000 ceramic filters to reduce firewood use. Both countries signed the agreement at the COP31 summit.

stories.title: Political restrictions deny Palestinians access to international environmental funding
stories.summary: The head of the Palestinian Environmental Quality Authority stated at COP31 that political restrictions are preventing access to international environmental funding. Despite full membership in relevant conventions, the official noted that projects are being denied support for non-technical reasons.

stories.title: S. Korea advances GVCM scheme with 8 partner countries
stories.summary: South Korea has advanced its global verified carbon market scheme as eight countries signed statements of interest at COP31. The government plans to launch a credit issuing body and has agreed to purchase up to 200,000 carbon credits under the framework.

stories.title: DRC to relaunch carbon market after passing key bill
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing to relaunch its carbon market following the passage of new legislation. The environment minister discussed the initiative during the COP31 climate summit. The country is seeking to establish a new regulatory framework for carbon trading.

stories.title: Bangladesh signs carbon market MoU with Singapore at COP31 - Daily Observer
Bangladesh and Singapore sign MoU on carbon market cooperation
stories.summary: Bangladesh and Singapore have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to cooperate on international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The agreement was signed at the COP31 summit in Turkiye to create new opportunities for climate finance and emissions reduction.

stories.title: Bangladesh, Singapore sign MoU on carbon market cooperation
stories.summary: Bangladesh and Singapore have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to enhance cooperation in international carbon markets. The agreement, signed at COP31, aims to open new opportunities for climate financing and joint initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

stories.summary: Singapore has authorised its first carbon credit project under a bilateral agreement with Rwanda. The project involves distributing 300,000 water filters to reduce firewood use and emissions. It aims to mitigate around 780,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030. stories.summary: ANTALYA, Turkey to Carbon-tax liable firms in Singapore could soon buy carbon credits from a water purification project in Rwanda to shrink their tax bill. stories.title: Saint Lucia PM calls for climate financing at COP31
stories.summary: Prime Minister Philip J. Pierre urged world leaders at COP31 to honour climate commitments and improve access to financing. He highlighted local impacts including crop loss and unreliable water supplies, warning that vulnerable nations cannot continue to bear the costs of a crisis they did not create.

stories.title: Australian minister calls for multilateralism at COP31
stories.summary: Australian Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen described the current global environment as a polycrisis. He stated that COP31 must demonstrate that multilateralism can still deliver results. The goal is to send a clear message to businesses that governments remain committed to supporting renewable energy investment.

stories.summary: DW News.. Thousands of climate activists have taken to the streets in Antalya, where Turkey is hosting the UN climate summit COP31. The march comes halfway through the negotiations to and marks a rare moment of large-scale public protest in Turkey. #dwn Facebook

stories.title: UN climate chief urges negotiators to avoid delays
stories.summary: UN climate chief Simon Stiell has urged negotiators at COP31 to move swiftly to the hardest issues and avoid tactical delays. With the conference at its midpoint, Stiell called for compromise from nearly 200 countries to reach goals on electrification and climate finance for vulnerable nations.

stories.title: Thousands rally against COP31 as talks hit midpoint
stories.summary: Thousands of protesters marched in Antalya on Nov 14 to accuse the climate summit of failing those affected by environmental destruction. Negotiators are scrambling to strike a deal by Nov 20, though the summit is not expected to produce a major breakthrough on fossil fuel curbs.

stories.title: Around 10,000 protest in Antalya during COP31
stories.summary: Approximately 10,000 people marched in Antalya to demand greater climate justice during COP31. Participants called on industrialized nations to increase funding for climate adaptation. The march took place about a half-hour drive from the summit venue, with activists carrying banners and puppets to express their frustration.

stories.title: Australia balances climate ambition and political reality
stories.summary: Australia is attempting to position itself as a global climate player at COP31 with a focus on the Pacific. The government is trying to demonstrate leadership while avoiding firm promises on fossil fuels. This pragmatism has left the country open to accusations that it is avoiding difficult questions.

stories.title: COP31 Day 6: Negotiations Gather Pace as Countries Prepare for Final Week - Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC)
UN climate chief calls for compromise at COP31
stories.summary: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell urged negotiators to avoid tactical delays as COP31 reached its halfway mark. He noted that getting agreement on every word is vital work. The conference continues through Nov 20, with a focus on bridging international agreements and the real economy.

stories.title: COP31: Protesters, UN urge swift climate deal
stories.summary: November 14, 2026 The United Nations' top climate official urged negotiators at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey to "avoid tactical delays" that would prevent a deal to stop global warming. stories.title: LGBTQ+ activists march at COP31 in Turkey
stories.summary: LGBTQ+ protesters marched in Antalya on Saturday during a civil society climate event. Despite a recent crackdown on LGBTQ+ rights in Turkey, campaigners from around the world formed a cordon around the activists. One participant noted that holding a rainbow flag in the city feels a bit dangerous.

stories.title: UAE expands recycling and resource recovery initiatives
stories.summary: The UAE is increasing recycling and resource recovery projects to support a circular economy. Initiatives in 2026 include biofuel production from used cooking oil and organic waste processing. The efforts aim to reduce landfill disposal and improve resource efficiency by converting waste into valuable economic and environmental assets.

stories.title: Mintoo for mainstreaming waste management into climate action - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
India's EPR framework shifts plastic waste costs to producers
stories.summary: India's Extended Producer Responsibility framework requires producers, importers and brand owners to manage plastic packaging after sale. Under the 2016 rules, the policy seeks to shift costs from municipalities to businesses to promote circularity. PIBOs must now meet collection and recycling obligations via a digital portal.

stories.title: Rethinking food waste in India's solid waste rules
stories.summary: India's waste-management framework is evolving to address food waste, which currently ends up in landfills despite traditional household habits. Experts suggest prioritising prevention and redistribution over conventional disposal. Packaged food waste is already subject to Extended Producer Responsibility rules under the existing Plastic Waste Management framework.

stories.title: Sachin Tendulkar invests in waste management firm Recykal
stories.summary: Cricket player Sachin Tendulkar has acquired a minority stake in Hyderabad-based Recykal. The investment is part of a 23 million dollar bridge funding round for the technology firm, which aims to promote circular economy practices. New investors also include the family office of Biological E Ltd.

stories.title: Roswall confirms single point EPR reporting
stories.summary: Roswall has confirmed that EPR reporting will move to a single point system under the Circular Economy Act. The change is intended to streamline how environmental directives are interpreted by member states. The system aims to identify pitfalls in current reporting requirements.

New York is running out of room for its waste even with Statue of Liberty-sized landfill
stories.summary: As a visual representation of how New York is running out of places to put its waste, the largest active landfill in the state is a striking one. The hulking Seneca Meadows landfill is already the height of the Statue of Liberty and its operators are seeking to raise it

stories.title: BME launches circular economy engineering programme
stories.summary: BME has introduced an MSc programme in Design and Development Engineering for a Circular Economy. The course aims to teach students how to transform production and consumption systems to use fewer resources. It combines engineering expertise to create more competitive and sustainable solutions for future industrial systems.

stories.title: Ministry of Mines concludes Special Campaign 6.0
stories.summary: The Ministry of Mines conducted Special Campaign 6.0 from 2 to 31 October to focus on e-waste management and administrative efficiency. The drive, organised by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, seeks to institutionalise cleanliness and ensure government resources are utilised effectively.

stories.title: AZTI wins award for circular economy fishing project
stories.summary: AZTI received the Waste Lab Bizkaia award for its work on the SEARCULAR project. The initiative coordinates fishing fleets, ports and recycling companies to repurpose disused fishing nets and gear. The award recognises efforts to reduce waste generated by fishing equipment at the end of its life.

stories.title: E.ON issues 1.8 billion euros in green bonds
stories.summary: E.ON has issued 1.8 billion euros in green bonds to cover its 2026 financing requirements. The issue consists of a seven-year note at 4.26 percent and an eleven-year tranche at 4.59 percent. The company says its funding for the year is now fully covered.

stories.title: E.ON reaffirms 2026 targets after profit rise
stories.summary: E.ON reaffirmed its 2026 targets after reporting a 4 percent increase in nine-month net income to 2.2 billion euros. The utility's EBITDA remained flat at 7.1 billion euros. The confirmation follows a recent downgrade by Morgan Stanley and the company's latest green bond issuance.

stories.title: Beko Calls for Climate, Trade, and Finance Policies to Align as Carbon Rules Reshape Manufacturing - StreetInsider
COP31 focuses on fossil fuel phase-out and grid bottlenecks
stories.summary: The second day of COP31 in Antalya focused on moving away from fossil fuels and addressing infrastructure barriers. Brazil presented a roadmap for transitioning from fossil fuels, while the UN issued a warning regarding global grid bottlenecks. Countries also discussed speeding up clean energy deployment.

stories.title: Microsoft May Abandon its Clean Energy Powered Data Centre Targets - EnergyNow.com
US data centre power demand outpaces grid capacity
stories.summary: US data centre power demand is growing ten times faster than grid capacity, according to research. Developers face delays and financial penalties, leading some operators to bypass public utilities for behind-the-meter generation. Insurers are now beginning to price the risks associated with these independent energy supplies.

stories.title: Sembcorp Green Infra receives SEBI nod for IPO
stories.summary: Sembcorp Green Infra has received final observations from SEBI for a proposed 3.75 billion rupee initial public offering. The Temasek-backed company intends to use the capital to strengthen its balance sheet. The firm operates projects combining solar, wind and energy storage technologies.

stories.title: BASF to power European PIB production with renewables
stories.summary: BASF aims to power its European polyisobutene production entirely with renewable electricity starting January 2027. The company will use long-term power purchase agreements, existing investments and external procurement to cover its Oppanol B and Glissopal portfolios. The transition follows a growing industry trend to reduce value chain emissions.

stories.title: Fourth Partner Energy signs ₹2,000 crore deal in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: Fourth Partner Energy signed a memorandum of understanding with the Andhra Pradesh government to develop three renewable energy projects. The plans include two solar plants and one hybrid wind-solar installation. The company already operates solar projects in the state for commercial and industrial customers.

stories.title: Equinix completes EUR 2.5 billion green bond issue
stories.summary: Equinix issued EUR 2.5 billion in green senior notes across four tranches to finance or refinance sustainability projects. The company updated its framework to cover green buildings, renewable energy, efficiency and water resilience. Investors are now watching for the execution of future infrastructure projects.

stories.title: RBC moves climate team to public policy unit
stories.summary: Royal Bank of Canada eliminated at least three senior climate and ESG roles while moving its remaining climate team into a new public policy group. Emily Head will lead the unit, which covers AI, payments and climate. The bank is currently reorganizing its internal structure.

stories.title: Nuveen Natural Capital launches combined nature-based investment vehicle
stories.summary: Nuveen Natural Capital launched a global nature-based solutions strategy with a $100 million anchor investment from its parent company, TIAA. The vehicle combines farmland, timberland, environmental markets and ecosystem restoration into one strategy. It will focus primarily on investments in the United States, Australia and Europe.
